idiom_name: fs/promises spill plus crypto.randomUUID() token (worker_threads for same-process hand-off)
implementation_notes: Node provides the primitives, not the component: write the payload with fs/promises (writeFile or createWriteStream) into a store directory or an object store, generate an unguessable key with crypto.randomUUID(), publish only the key, and delete the object in the consumer for claim-once semantics - there is no Check Luggage step to configure, so the extraction and redemption code is yours. Where producer and consumer are threads of the same process the payload never has to be copied at all: an ArrayBuffer can be transferred through postMessage and a SharedArrayBuffer is shared by reference, which is the honest claim check over shared memory. The store-and-token form is still the right choice whenever the message must survive a restart, because thread-local buffers and transferable arrays die with the process.
pitfalls: Keys become part of the security surface: a randomUUID is unguessable, but a path built from user input can escape the store directory (../ traversal), so validate and join paths deliberately.
A local directory is node-local: the consumer may run on another replica, find nothing and fail as if the payload had been deleted - use an object store as soon as more than one process consumes.

Transferring an ArrayBuffer moves ownership, so the sender's view is detached and reading it afterwards fails; a SharedArrayBuffer needs explicit coordination (Atomics) because there is no queueing semantics.
Unredeemed payloads accumulate: without an unlink step or a lifecycle rule on the store, the temp volume fills up and the first symptom appears in an unrelated service.
